column1: NUCCESS Recommendation Rules Engine  -  Simplified Matrix

One-sheet developer view: what the user supplies on the left, what the engine returns on the right. Six worked scenarios for each of the 16 State Grid cells, varying emotion, intensity, context and demand, so the same state can be seen producing different outputs. Built from Tabs 1-9 and the v2 Architecture & Screen Specification (30 Aug 2026). The source tabs remain the authority and are unchanged.

Read a row left to right: STATE (Tab 1) + EXPERIENCE (Tab 2, sensations per screen S09) + CONTEXT (screen S10 - environment, social, time/transition, available support) gives INTERVENTION SEQUENCE (Tab 2 domains filtered by Tab 3) and RECOMMENDATION (Tab 7 CTA). Every rationale follows one shape: Because <your state> and <what you're feeling>, Nuccess <what it suggests>. <what comes next>.

column1: SENSATION CATEGORIES  (screen S09)  -  six categories. Sensations are OPTIONAL, multi-select, and may carry their own intensity. Pain is a Body sensation, not an emotion.

column5: How the environment is landing: sound sensitivity, light glare or flicker, visual overload, texture discomfort, smell, temperature.
What thinking feels like: brain fog, thought-looping, gone blank, slowed processing, too many open threads, hyperfocus lock.
What the body reports: PAIN (with its own intensity), heaviness, chest tightness, jaw or shoulder tension, stomach churn, ache, numbness, head pressure, tingling.
What speech and language feel like: word-retrieval gaps, speech feels effortful, cannot sequence sentences, going non-verbal.
What the body wants to do: restlessness, fidget urge, need to pace, stimming urge, foot-tapping, feeling frozen in place.

The body's internal signals: hunger, thirst, needing the toilet, sleepiness or tiredness, feeling too hot or too cold, heartbeat awareness. Differences in interoception mean these are often missed, so NUCCESS asks directly. (v3.1)

column1: CONTEXT DIMENSIONS  (screen S10 / architecture layer 4)  -  context FILTERS which tools are realistic. It never changes WHICH intervention is chosen.

column5: The physical setting: lecture hall, library, seminar room, exam hall, placement ward, open-plan office, focus booth, lab, co-working space, client site, conference floor, commute, halls, shared flat, home desk.
Who else is present and what they require: alone, strangers nearby, team within earshot, spoken contribution expected, presenting to a group, invigilated, supervising clinician present.
Time of day and the transition being crossed: start of shift, between lectures, post-lunch dip, pre-meeting run-up, end of day, commute, exam underway, sustained over weeks.
What help is actually reachable right now: trusted contacts, AI or human body double, bookable quiet room, tutor, mentor or manager, recorded lecture, granted extra time, wellbeing service.
Tab 3a - Sound, Noise, Lights, Crowd. Multi-select, separate from Sensations. Narrows tools WITHIN the chosen intervention.

column1: THE SUPPORT PATHWAYS  (Tab 2 / spec S6)  -  eight confirmed in v3.2: Regulate, Express, Execute, Dump, Adapt, Reflect, Connect, Meditate (Rituals / Prayer). Support-side output. Regulate is a pathway, NOT a driver.

column5: How can I feel, sense or function better right now? Sensory reduction, grounding, breathing, movement, pause, attention reset, recovery. The default forced-first step under distress.
Too much in my head and I cannot organise or name it. Text/voice capture, externalisation, optional sorting AFTER capture. Nothing auto-converts into a task.
I know what I mean but cannot get it into words or structure. Draft, rewrite, simplify, script. Always user-approved; never auto-sends.
I feel isolated, or I want social or community contact. Trusted person, async contact, low-demand participation, body doubling.
I have something to do but do not know how to start. Smallest next action, sequencing, breakdown, focus support. Step count capped by the Timeline code.
The current way of doing this is creating unnecessary friction. Change environment, modality, sequence, scope, pace - never frame masking as adaptation.

Help me make sense of what happened, or what helped. Short, guided, time-limited prompts (what happened, what helped, what I'd keep or change); optional saving to My Patterns. Offered in Green, Blue, and Yellow at Mild/Moderate intensity. Amber: 'save for later'. Red or rumination: Dump or Regulate first (pattern 40). Distinct from Dump (unstructured offload) and Express (words for someone else).

Help me find stillness, or keep the practice that grounds me. Intentional practice chosen by the user: stillness, guided settling, gratitude, opening/closing rituals, and the user's own prayer times or recitations. Short breath and grounding micro-tools stay in Regulate. Never infers faith; never replaces support. Gates MD-1 to MD-6 in Tab 6c.

column1: THE REGULATE TOOLKIT  (Tab 3b / screen S15)  -  these are the tool names used in the “Tools left after the context filter” column above.

column5: Paced breathing. The most portable tool - discreet, works seated or standing, needs no equipment and nobody can tell. Never excluded by any context in Tab 3b.
Sensory grounding, usually 5-4-3-2-1. Subtle and can be done eyes-open, so it survives meetings, exam halls and packed carriages.

Physical discharge: walking, pacing, stretching, shaking out. The tool restlessness responds to - and the one that needs space and social permission, so it is the first thing any observed or public setting excludes.
Audio regulation. Fine anywhere it can be routed through headphones; excluded wherever external audio would carry to other people.
Drawing, making, tactile work. Visible by nature, so excluded in formal, observed or public settings even though it is otherwise low-demand.
Leave the room for one or two minutes. Tab 3b calls this the “step-outside micro-action”. The fallback when Move is indicated but the setting will not allow it.
The remaining two families named in spec S6. Not yet broken out by context in Tab 3b - worth completing before build.

column1: THE EIGHT DRIVERS  (Tab 5 / spec S5)  -  demand-side output. Only ever applied when a demand exists.

column5: New, unfamiliar, different, or offering a new experience.
Real time pressure with a consequence for delay. Derived from the Timeline code, never user-labelled.
Requires problem-solving, sustained effort, complexity or stretch.
Familiar, predictable, structured, low decision cost.
Naturally captures attention, curiosity or engagement.
Connected to personal meaning, values or enthusiasm.

The activity itself involves social participation with others or within a group. NOT the same as the Connect intervention: Connect asks what support I need for social connection; this asks whether the ACTIVITY is with others.

column1: CAPACITY BANDS AND TRAFFIC LIGHTS  (Tab 1 baseline, adjusted by Tab 10)  -  Green / Yellow / Amber / muted Red, plus Blue for Recovery.

column5: No intervention required. Go straight to the demand if one exists.
Light or optional intervention offered first. Never blocking - “Skip to task” stays visible.
Intervention is the forced primary. Demand capped to Routine until a re-check improves the state.

column1: Very Constrained ( Red traffic light: use muted red and not bright red colour)
column5: Intervention forced immediately. Demand deferred entirely. Support pathway visible throughout.

Overlay, not a band: shown when a Yellow, Amber or Red user completes support and the re-check improves. Demand stays gentle for the recovery window; the band then rises one step per re-check (Tab 10 RC-1 to RC-5).

column1: TIMELINE CODES  (Tab 4)  -  feeds the Urgency driver ONLY. Never touches Energy or Mood, and is never stored as part of State.

column5: Urgency at maximum. Execute capped to 1-3 micro-steps. Shortens a needed Regulate step to 1-2 min - never skips it.
Urgency high. Execute capped to 3-5 steps. Body Double defaults to AI (no lead time to invite a person).
Urgency moderate. Fuller breakdown allowed. Body Double can offer “invite a colleague or friend”.
Urgency low. Challenge / Exploration may outrank minimum-viable-action.
As T3. Routine / Interest-led planning favoured over urgency.
Urgency effectively inactive. Exploration / Interest-led if the user wants to engage now.
Urgency not applicable. Driven entirely by State + Intervention + the other drivers.
Deadline has passed. Repair first: a short, factual message (explain, ask for more time), then the smallest remaining step. No blame language.
Repeats on a schedule (daily, weekly). Urgency comes from the next occurrence; strengthens the Routine driver.

column1: NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES  -  apply to every row above, without exception  (Tab 7 footer / spec S11, S15).
•   Never present more than one primary CTA plus a small number of alternatives. Never a long menu.
•   “Not now” / rejection is always a valid, unpenalised outcome. Log it, but do not repeat the same rejected suggestion immediately.
•   Timeline can SHORTEN a Regulate step but never skip a genuinely needed one, and never overrides a Support pathway.
•   The user never sees the Energy-Mood grid, the word “Intervention”, or the driver acronym. They see the state name, icon and meaning, one plain-language CTA, and the rationale.
•   The Support pathway (the SOS row) is never hidden, demoted, or replaced by an alternative.
•   Do not manufacture a task where there is no demand. The intervention pathway can be the complete response - even at Peak Flow (see E4M4.6).
•   High sensory load triggers environmental adaptation BEFORE increasing demand, even when the band is Available (see E2M4.6, E3M4.1, E4M4.5).
•   Every numeric threshold here is an MVP starting point and should be tunable configuration, not hard-coded.
